question: Solving x² - 6·x + 5 = 0, smaller root is 1 m/s. With 130 kg, force = 130 N, scaled by 9, increased by 3, scaled by 10, converted to kiloNewtons. The tenant ID is t99, not used. What is the final force in kiloNewtons?

The quantity to find is a total energy in kJ for 11 identical drones, each contributing its energy of motion less 1 J of rotor-hub friction. A drone has a mass of 44000 g. Starting from rest at t = 3 s, its acceleration from t = 3 s to t = 4 s is 2t² + 2t, in m/s², with t in seconds; at t = 4 s a boost doubles its speed, and the energy of motion is taken at the doubled speed. Add up the 11 drones' contributions in J and convert to kJ. What is the total, in kJ?

The derivative of 4x^3 + 2x^2 at x = 1 is 8. Decreasing by 15 gives -7, scaled by 4 to get -28. A 33 kg mass has kinetic energy from 784, converted to kJ, scaled by 6. A drag coefficient is not used. What is the final energy in kJ?

The final number a model-rocket sled test track crew logs, in kilojoules, is 6 more than an earlier figure, which is itself 16 more than a kilojoule reading converted from an energy value that had been multiplied by 6. The unmultiplied energy, in joules, is what a 4 kilogram sled carries while moving at a speed equal to how sharply the sled's motion is changing at t = 4 seconds, given that its position, in meters, follows s(t) = 2t^3 - 2t^2 for t in seconds after launch. What is the final number, in kilojoules?
The calculation 3*(5 + 20) = 75 m/s^2. A 63 kg mass produces force = 4725 N, converted to kN, decreased by 23, scaled by 12, decreased by 13. A limit is 100 kN. What is the final force in kN?

A spring mechanism has parameters satisfying x^2 - 11x + 24 = 0; use the larger root. Multiply by 4, add 6 to get the effective spring constant. With a 3-kilogram mass at this constant (as acceleration in m/s²), calculate energy. Scale by 8 for oscillations. The spring material is stainless steel, not needed. What is the oscillation energy in J?

Solve x² - 14x + 48 = 0, choose larger root. A motor with mass 128 kilograms runs at this acceleration. Calculate force. Subtract 9. Scale by 2. Scale by 9. Subtract 9. What is the final force in Newtons?

A laboratory needs the final entry, in kilojoules, for a spring-launcher trial. The launcher's raw index is the area under the curve 2*x^2 + 7*x between x = 1 and x = 2, where x is the cam setting. The calibration then subtracts 20 from that raw index and adds a further 13 to what remains, and the result is the projectile's launch speed in metres per second. The projectile has a mass of 4 kg, and the bench sits at 21 degrees C. The entry records the energy the projectile carries by virtue of that motion. What is the final entry, in kJ?

A launcher accelerates a sled of 51000 grams from rest along a level track, and its acceleration in metres per second squared follows 3t^2 + 5t between t = 0 seconds and t = 2 seconds, with t measured from release. At the end of that interval the logger records the energy the sled carries because of its motion and expresses it in kilojoules. A fixed instrument offset of 24 kJ is added to the converted value, and the sum is multiplied by 7 because the programme calls for 7 identical launches. From that programme total a calibration credit of 23 kJ is subtracted to give the certified number. The track's guard rail is 30 m long and plays no part. What is the certified number, in kilojoules?

A force system is governed by the first derivative of 2 times x cubed minus 4 times x squared, evaluated at x equals 3 seconds, giving an instantaneous rate. From this rate, subtract 18 units, then subtract 8 more units to get an effective acceleration. A 131-kilogram structural member experiencing this acceleration develops force proportional to mass times acceleration in Newtons. Multiply by 11, then multiply by 11 again to get the maximum design force. The system's height was 5 meters but does not enter the force calculation. What is the maximum design force in Newtons?

A quarry report closes with one number in kilonewtons. A skip whose mass plate reads 159000 g is accelerated up the incline. Its acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the exact area under the curve y = 4x^2 + 0x between x = 2 and x = 3. The haul rope must supply the force that gives that skip that acceleration, and 3 N of that force is taken up by the guide roller and subtracted. The remainder is written in kilonewtons, after which two corrections are added in those same kilonewton units: 2 for the drum offset and 25 for the standing preload. The quarry pond holds 800 L of water, which is no part of this. What number closes the report, in kN?

Two cable offcuts measure 14 cm and 130 cm; the greatest length dividing both evenly is used as the acceleration, in m/s², of a machine part whose mass is stated as 96000 grams. A separate voltage reading of 230 V on the control panel is not needed here. The resulting force is converted into kilonewtons, scaled by a factor of 6, and finally increased by 17 kN. What is the final force, in kilonewtons?

A 108 kg robot is accelerated across a factory floor at a rate, in m/s², equal to the area under the curve y = 4x² + 4x from x = 0 to x = 1. A slope supplies 19 N of the force needed, and a cable adds 3 N of drag. The factory runs 6 identical robots per line and 9 lines. What total force, in N, must the drives supply?

A lab's final reading, in kilojoules after a sixfold scaling, is the target number — but everything starts with two small speed readings. Two probe speeds of 4 m/s and 5 m/s are added together and the sum doubled, giving the effective speed of a test slider. That speed belongs to a slider whose mass is listed as 16000 grams. From the resulting kinetic energy, 10 J is subtracted for a friction correction, and the corrected value is converted into kilojoules. Finally, the converted energy is scaled by a factor of six to represent six repeated trials. What is the final energy, in kilojoules?

A quadratic solver finds the larger root of x² - 13x + 40 = 0 (which is 8 m/s). An 8 kg mass yields energy, increased by 12 J, scaled by 5, converted to kilojoules, and reduced by 22 kJ. What is the final energy in kilojoules?
Calculate 2 × (8 + 20) = 56. With 57 kg, force = 3192 N, convert to 3.192 kN, minus 8 → -4.808, plus 26. The device rating is 5000 W. What is the final force in kN?

The figure the freight-yard controller wants is the total energy in kilojoules for 6 identical trains, each of 7 identical wagons. Each wagon in the yard's scale model has a mass of 31 kg and moves at a speed in metres per second found by taking 8 times the sum of 4 and 3 and then adding 14. Find the kinetic energy of one wagon in joules, multiply by 7 for one train, then by 6 for all the trains, and convert the total to kilojoules. What is the total in kJ?

A test carriage on a rail rig has a mass of 157 kilograms. The carriage's speed, in meters per second, t seconds after launch, follows the pattern 5 times t squared plus 4 times t; engineers need the total distance the carriage covers between t = 2 seconds and t = 3 seconds, and use that total distance as the carriage's acceleration, in meters per second squared. Using that acceleration and the carriage's mass, a certain force is found. A calibration offset then subtracts 21 from that force. The result, in newtons, is converted into kilonewtons, a further loss of 6 is subtracted, and a final gain of 15 is added. The rail yard has 5 loading docks. What is the resulting force, in kilonewtons?

A theme park's water ride meters its pump through a surge, and at time t seconds the meter's instantaneous rate is 2 times t squared plus 8 times t. A boat's speed, in metres per second, equals the total that meter accumulates between the 2nd and the 3rd second. The boat has a mass of 12000 g on the scale model used for the estimate, and the ride's queue canopy is 40 m long. Nine boats run at once, and the ride sheet then subtracts 5 J absorbed by the brake pads. Expressed in kilojoules, the park's total then adds 19 kJ drawn by the pump house. What is the park's total, in kJ?

A flow system's velocity is determined by the definite integral of 3 times x squared plus 2 times x, integrated from x equals 0 to x equals 1, then scaled by multiplying by 3. A 23-kilogram fluid mass at this scaled velocity develops kinetic energy as half mass times velocity squared. Subtract 25 Joules, subtract 13 Joules, and multiply by 6 to find the net energy. What is the net energy in Joules?

A laboratory report ends with a value that is 5 times a site figure, because 5 laboratories report together. Each site figure is what you get by adding a standing instrument allowance of 29 kJ to a converted reading. That converted reading is the kilojoule form of the energy a glider of 38 kg carries because of its motion along the air track, and the glider's speed in metres per second is the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 10x + 24 = 0. The track is 2 m long, a dimension the report never uses. What value, in kilojoules, ends the report?

The definite integral of 2*x^2 + 8*x from 0 to 3 equals 54. A 4-kilogram object with acceleration 54 m/s^2 experiences force. Convert from newtons to kilonewtons, add 19, subtract 2, and multiply by 6. What is the final force in kilojoules?

A stress profile s(x) = 2x^2 (integrated from x=1 to x=3) yields total. An 108 kg specimen (or 108000 grams) produces force. After converting to kN, scaling by 12, 8, and 12, what is the final force in kilonewtons?

A calibration check for a flywheel's speed sensor requires two numbers whose sum is 5 and whose product is 6; engineers use the smaller of the two, then add 29, to get the true speed in meters per second. This is the speed of a 35 kg flywheel; find its kinetic energy, multiply by 4 for a four-flywheel bank, subtract 18 joules for a calibration offset, and add back 25 joules for a separate correction. A separate tachometer on the bank reads 1500 rpm, unrelated to this calculation. What is the final energy, in joules?

A tram engineer needs the final force rating, in kilonewtons, for a bogie: the force to accelerate a 121 000 g test carriage, less 6 N recovered by a regenerative unit, plus 26 N for coupler drag, expressed in kilonewtons. The acceleration, in m/s², is 21 more than the area under the curve y = 1·x² + 6x from x = 2 to x = 4. What is the final rating, in kN?
